question: Do first-party VISION3 50D, 250D and 500T diffuse-rms granularity shapes provide a stock-distinguishing source-domain signature independent of the already-identified MTF diversity?

comparison.metric: RMSE of natural-log diffuse-rms Sigma-D after subtracting each stock-channel mean on the common exposure grid
comparison.interpolation: linear in log-relative exposure and natural-log Sigma-D
comparison.negative_control: the exact one-Gaussian MTF compiler must remain closed; granularity diversity cannot rescue or relabel its failed representation

allowed_after_pass: retain a three-stock source-domain granularity signature alongside the independent MTF signature
freeze a separate source-prior bundle that serializes observed MTF and granularity curves without yet selecting microscopic NPS or photographic placement
forbidden: change trace pixels, common exposures, normalization, metric or gates after pairwise scoring
use granularity diversity to rescue the failed BU1 one-Gaussian MTF compiler
infer microscopic grain size, NPS, roll/process/scanner calibration or digital RGB appearance
render photographs, train a router or alter B0/AO6 from this source result

branch_rule.pass: Retain source-domain granularity diversity and open only a typed observed-source profile bundle.
branch_rule.fail: Close these exact VISION3 granularity traces without trace, stock, exposure, threshold or normalization rescue.

claim_ceiling: First-party manufacturer-graph diffuse-rms granularity diversity at one stated 48-micrometre aperture for three VISION3 stocks; not NPS, microscopic structure, roll/process/scanner calibration, photographic appearance or product evidence.
